title: Amit Shah and ECI claim SIR Was to Catch ‘Infiltrators’. Commission Has no Record of Them
authors: Ayushi Kar (edited by Mayank Aggarwal, visual by Nitin Sethi)
shows: From its RTI applications and its reporting on the Commission's software, the Collective finds that the SIR gave officers no way to record anyone as a foreigner. The Commission passed its questions on cases referred under the Citizenship Act to Bihar alone, and the two Bihar replies it reproduces give the names left off by reason with no category for people who are not citizens. It sets this beside the Home Minister's statement that the Leader of the Opposition was protecting infiltrators.
quote: But our investigation into the ECI’s software and the Commission’s response to our Right to Information (RTI) Act applications shows the ECI had no mechanism or process to tag any of the 13.39 crore deleted voters as ‘foreigners’.
Its software did not provide an option for officials across the states to identify and mark people as foreigners.
Over 100 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) in Bihar responded to our RTI application and confirmed this.
Instead of replying to our request, the Commission forwarded our questions to merely one state — Bihar.
We investigated the election officers' software, ERONET, removing voters first-hand. We found there was no option to mark voters as non-Indians.
note: Opened on 19 October 2026 with curl (200, full text in the page, free to read). Byline Ayushi Kar, edited by Mayank Aggarwal, visual by Nitin Sethi, published and updated 16 October 2026. The RTI replies are in rti_research/rti.json as rti-14 and rti-15. The article's '13.39 crore deleted voters' is the site's count of names left off the drafts (13,39,03,307, data/india/states.json total.removed), which on the site's terms were left off and were not deleted. The article's statement that the SIR 'contained no procedure to detect and delete voters on the grounds of them being non-citizens' is its reading of the Commission's instructions for phase 2 and of ERONET; the instruction it shows (para 2(a), 'BLO may identify a probable cause, such as Absent/Shifted/Death/Duplicate') is reproduced as an image. The Bengal welfare cut and the Chief Minister's statement it cites are not carried in 'shows'.

title: The ECI Software Deleted 5.38 Lakh Bengal Voters With Auto-Generated Rejections Without Citing a Reason
shows: Reads the Form 10 registers published with West Bengal's final roll for 284 of the 294 constituencies and finds 5,23,998 names deleted on Form 7s that give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 confirms that the state's Form 7 figure of 5,38,320 included forms the Commission's software generated when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing. It sets these deletions by district, by the party that won each seat and against the 2026 margins.
quote: Records show that as many as 5,38,320 voters have been struck off West Bengal’s final electoral roll through Form 7 objections without any person having filed them.

Of the 5,24,420 deletions The Wire could verify, in 5,23,998 rows – 99.9% of all Form 7-related deletions in these constituencies – the objector is the ERO, and the reason column is left blank in every single case.
This does not mean every one of these voters was wrongly removed. Many may well have been ineligible.
Speaking to The Wire, Arindam Niyogi, the Additional CEO – West Bengal said that the Form 10 does not provide the option to give details.
In six of the 283 seats covered by the registers that The Wire was able to check for form 7 deletions, the ‘no reason’ deletions were more than the winning margin itself.
note: Opened on 19 October 2026 with curl at m.thewire.in (200, full text, free). Published 17 October 2026, 8:00 am IST. The brief named it as possibly with @chhuti_is; the byline is Aparna Bhattacharya alone and no co-author or partner is credited on the page. Also entered as soft-32 in disputes_research/software.json. Inconsistencies to check: 'Only 7,733 of the Form 7 rejections because a person actually filed the form' against its count of 422 individual objectors in 284 seats, and 5.46 lakh in one place for the 5.38 lakh. 'Shows' leaves out the article's name-based guess at religion and its 150-seat comparison of the overall fall with the margins. Deletions here are names taken off after the draft, which the site calls deleted.

title: Inside India’s electoral overhaul that removed 130mn voters
shows: The Financial Times reports critics' view that the review wrongly took eligible voters off the rolls, many of them Muslim, and may have helped the Prime Minister's party. Only the headline and standfirst could be read.
quote: Critics say ‘aggressive’ review wrongly removed eligible voters, many of them Muslim, and may have benefited PM Modi’s party
note: Not read in full: ft.com answers with its subscription page (HTTP 403, 'Subscribe to read', isAccessibleForFree False), WebFetch is refused for ft.com, and the Wayback Machine refused the request (429). What was read: the page's JSON-LD and meta tags give the headline 'Inside India’s electoral overhaul that removed 130mn voters', authors Andres Schipani and Jyotsna Singh, published 2026-10-15T21:00:04Z (16 October, 2:30 am IST), modified 2026-10-16T08:03:37Z, and the standfirst quoted above; Schipani's FT author feed lists the same piece as 'How India deleted more than 130mn voters'.
